experiment: Exp 19B: Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B on the Exp18 64-layer causal Qwen3.8-27B oracle, with BiasCorr gates

corpus.special_token_note: Qwen tokenizer has add_bos_token=False and bos_token_id=None; rows are raw text windows, matching prior verified Qwen experiments. Position 0 is excluded from calibration means regardless.
corpus.window_layout: raw 512-token windows; positions 1..511 scored; 4 rows/domain = 2044 targets
corpus.calibration_layout: 4 x WikiText-2 TRAIN tail walking backward + 4 x _pydecimal.py walking forward from token 512; all means exclude position 0
corpus.overlap_6gram_note: rows keys use row-local n-grams; flattened keys include cross-window n-grams inside each contiguous eval stream. Every key must be exactly zero before any calibration row is accepted.

ood_chat.selection_note: round-robin gsm8k,mmlu,humaneval preserving frozen source order inside each suite; minimal prefix covering the eval windows
ood_chat.window_layout: first 4 contiguous 512-token windows; positions 1..511 scored (2044 targets); no padding

meta.scope:
Exp 19B: prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-mlx-2bit on the Exp18 causal BF16 oracle.

Format (config.json, hadamard.json, whitepaper 2.1-2.4): MLX affine 2-bit codes per
group of 128 with FP16 scale and bias, stored in a rotated basis. A packed linear
computes W_s @ H1024(signs * x), so the effective dense weight is
(W_s @ H1024) * signs. embed_tokens is stored the same way and inverse-rotated.
Norm convention: HF Qwen3_5RMSNorm computes x * (1 + w) and the BF16 checkpoint stores
w. The MLX pack stores the full scale, so every Qwen3_5RMSNorm weight is loaded as
w_bonsai - 1 (kept FP32). The gated GDN norm uses its weight directly in both.
The oracle substitutes that dense weight (BF16) into the same causal stream as Exp18.
It does not run PrismML's kernels and measures no speed.

BiasCorr variants (all one FP32 vector per decoder linear, 4,088 cal positions):
  BC_weight_diff     b = (W_bf16 - W_q) @ E[x_bf16]
  BC_act_resid       sequential output-mean matching: in execution order, on the
                     corrected quantized cal stream, b = E[y_bf16] - E[y_q].
  BC_act_resid_open  b = E[y_bf16] - E[y_q], y_q from the uncorrected quantized cal
                     stream (all upstream error is counted again at every layer).
With identical inputs E[y_bf16 - y_q] is algebraically BC_weight_diff, so the
residual variants differ only by using each model's own activations.

PTQ_samefmt is a control: MSE-optimal ternary of the BF16 weights in Bonsai's exact
format (same rotation, signs, group 128, same tensors left unquantized).

model.training_method: Not stated in the model card or the Bonsai 2 whitepaper read on 2026-11-25. 'QAT' is NOT a verified property.

dequant_checks.note: embed_tokens is audited on the rows used by this run only

causality_precheck_stock.method: three same-shape (3,128) streams: reference, exact rerun, row-2 future perturbed; gated diffs are same-slot
